source_neutral.procedure: The objects worked on are the surviving draft's leaves, sections, textual variants and apparent revision layers. The sequence in which these were revised and assembled is treated as partially unknown. Additional witnesses, correspondence and custody records are treated as possible sources of dated traces; their availability is not assumed. The working assumption under test is that traces can be securely associated with particular draft units or textual states. The overall process is: collect available traces, record what each trace identifies and what kind of date it carries, cross-check proposed transitions between textual states against several kinds of evidence, check whether records are independent of one another, arrange the supported transitions into a chronology expressed as exact dates, relative order or date ranges according to what the evidence supports, mark unsupported intervals as gaps, keep competing sequences where links conflict or are ambiguous, and report the result as a scoped hypothesis with stated assumptions.
source_neutral.action: 1) Gather available witnesses, material evidence, correspondence and archival provenance records. 2) For each trace, record which draft unit or textual state it identifies and whether its date concerns writing, copying, custody or assembly. 3) Cross-check each proposed transition using variants, deletions, insertions, handwriting, paper features and dated context. 4) Check whether records that appear to corroborate one another are independent or derive from a common source. 5) Arrange supported transitions into a chronology, using relative order or date ranges where exact dates are unsupported. 6) Keep the composition, revision, assembly and custody sequences distinct from one another, and do not substitute the order of the story's narrative for any of them. 7) Mark unsupported intervals as gaps. 8) Retain competing sequences where links conflict or remain ambiguous. 9) For an unresolved link, seek additional witnesses, material inspection, or relevant dated correspondence and provenance. 10) Stop extending that link when accessible evidence cannot distinguish the alternatives, and state what further evidence would be needed.
source_neutral.observables: Signals supporting a link: independent traces that identify the same draft units or textual states and impose compatible chronological constraints on the transitions between them. Illustrative case given in the mapping: a securely dated witness preserves one reading, a physically interpretable alteration changes that reading, and an independently dated later witness preserves the changed reading; together these could support a local revision sequence, subject to checks on copying and on identification. Signals for assembly links: compatible evidence that concerns the joining or ordering of units. Signals of an unresolved transition, as opposed to a completed sequence: conflicting dates, ambiguous identifications, records that depend on one another, and missing intermediate witnesses.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: Links that are compatible and independently supported justify a bounded reconstruction of the documented revision and assembly. A sequence is preferred to the extent that it accommodates the supported constraints without requiring unsupported transitions. If the evidence does not distinguish a complete history, the output is an ordered subset or a set of competing sequences. Each transition is classified as established within the available evidence, provisional, or unresolved. A dated witness can establish that a reading existed by that date, provided its identification and dating are secure; by itself it does not date when the reading was first composed. Evidence about custody or location constrains conclusions about how the text was formed solely where an additional supported link connects that evidence to revision or assembly.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: Units: draft units (leaves, sections), textual states, textual variants, and apparent revision layers of the surviving draft. Traces: witnesses, material evidence (handwriting, paper features, deletions, insertions, alterations), correspondence, and archival provenance or custody records. Attributes recorded per trace: which draft unit or textual state it identifies; the type of date it carries (writing, copying, custody or assembly); and whether it is independent of other records or derives from a common source. Relationships: transitions between textual states or units, each evaluated as an individual link; chronological constraints (exact dates, relative order, or date ranges) imposed on those transitions; joining or ordering relations among units for assembly. Four sequences are tracked separately: composition, revision, assembly and custody, with the story's narrative order kept apart from all four. Link statuses: established within available evidence, provisional, unresolved. Unsupported intervals are represented as gaps, and conflicting or ambiguous links are represented as retained competing sequences. Local revision sequences are distinguished from the formation of the whole work.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: For any unresolved link, the specified follow-up is to seek additional witnesses, material inspection, or relevant dated correspondence and provenance. Where extension of a link is stopped because accessible evidence cannot distinguish the alternatives, the follow-up is to state what further evidence would be needed to distinguish them. No further follow-up beyond these is specified.
source_neutral.limits: Conditions affecting the evidence: records and witnesses may be lost, inaccessible, anonymous, forged, mistaken, or copied from one another. Names, manuscript descriptions and draft-unit identifications may be ambiguous. Handwriting, paper and alteration evidence may permit several interpretations. Earlier readings may be recopied or restored, so a textual difference alone need not determine the direction of revision. Absence of a witness or record does not establish absence of revision, transfer or rearrangement. A chronology that appears continuous may contain undocumented or misidentified transitions. A local alteration cannot establish the formation of the whole work. Additional witnesses, correspondence and custody records are not assumed to be available, and the assumption that traces can be securely associated with particular draft units or textual states is itself under test. Stopping rule: extension of an unresolved link stops when accessible evidence cannot distinguish the alternatives, at which point the needed further evidence is stated. Reporting conditions: conclusions are reported as a scoped scholarly hypothesis with explicit assumptions about identity, dating, independence and direction of change. The packet establishes no actual sequence and no practitioner consensus.
